regression_check: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules-optout-identity.test.ts: 'CURRENT LIMITATION (ISS-T037W1-001)' asserts the miss as current behaviour
title: Opt-out follows the meeting only while the opted-out source record is still in the current selection; once it is absent, its sibling from another source still joins
evidence: applyJoinRules(sel([item g1 gmail, sessionKey gmail:g1, zoom 123456789]), {version:1,ownDomains:[],rules:[]}, {state:{approvedSenders:[],approvedDomains:[],optedOutEventIds:["calX"]}}) -> g1 stays scheduled. Concrete scenario: the person opts out of calendar event calX; on the next tick the Calendar fetch fails or returns without calX (event edited/deleted/outage, or calX is not due yet, which selectAutoRecordItems drops silently without a skipped row); the Gmail copy g1 of the same Zoom meeting is selected alone and joins unattended. Also: if calX was SKIPPED (skipped rows carry no URL) and g1 has a different start time (so a different webinar sessionKey) the only link is the URL identity, which a skipped row cannot supply.
fix_direction: Design (ii), store the meeting identity with the opt-out. State format change in join-rules.ts / join-rules-store.ts / the opt-out API route: JoinRuleState gains optedOutMeetings: string[] (values from send-now.ts meetingIdentity(url), e.g. "zoom:123456789"), validated like optedOutEventIds (non-empty strings, deduplicated, bounded); the opt-out API takes the meeting URL (or resolves it server side from the calendar event / gmail candidate it already loads) and records BOTH eventId and meetingIdentity via a new recordOptOut(state, eventId, meetingUrl?); version bump of the persisted state with a reader that accepts the old shape; applyJoinRules then vetoes any scheduled item whose meetingIdentity(item.meetingUrl) is in optedOutMeetings, with no dependence on the opted-out record being present. Single matcher stays evaluateJoinRules (add the identity check there). Owner lane needs packages/db / store / apps/api, which this lane may not touch.

title: Identity matching is conservative for recurring rooms: opting out of one instance also removes any other instance of the same Zoom/Meet room present in the same selection
evidence: Two scheduled items with the same platform meeting identity but different start times (e.g. a personal-room link used at 10:00 and 15:00): opt-out of the 10:00 id removes both. Removal-only, so safe for privacy; it can drop a wanted join. The extractor ignores start time by design.
fix_direction: Accepted for now (fail-closed). If it bites, link by identity only when start times are within a window, or move to design (ii) with identity plus start (ISS-T037W1-001).

title: Wiring and attention-alerts must handle opted-out / rule-denied / rules-unevaluable: operation-reason vocabularies elsewhere do not list them
evidence: Those lists are operation-reason vocabularies keyed on the existing SkipReason strings; none reads the three new values, and nothing emits them yet because applyJoinRules is unwired. When wiring persists skipped items as operations, run-pipeline.mjs's includes-list at :226 will not treat the new reasons as action-required.
fix_direction: Wiring unit: decide per consumer (action_required vs silent) and add the three values deliberately; attention-alerts lane must add them when merged.
